text:
mira: quick sync — thinking about adding an early gating layer in the obs stream to cut cost from a few noisy mobile apps. high level options: pre-filter at edge, sticky sampling, or strict per-client rate limits. which tradeoffs do folks worry about most? :thinking:

 todd: do we have recent numbers on what the top-n noisy clients contribute? wouldn't want to overoptimize without data.

 anika: we do — mobile client X accounted for ~22% of raw spans last week, but after enrichment it was only ~6% of billed traces. main risk is losing billing attribution when we drop early (clients often attach billing_key in late enrichment).

 kevin: +1 on the attribution risk. one pattern that worked elsewhere: prefilter on obviously malformed / duplicate payloads, then apply sticky sampling per device id for the rest. sticky_window gives us a chance to rehydrate with late-enrich keys if the event surfaces soon after.

 mira: that aligns with my thinking. malformed/dupe filter is cheap and safe. sticky sampling seems like the right middle ground compared to blunt rate-limits. can you sketch config?

 kevin: sure — pseudo-config below (edge proxy):
```yaml
gating:
  prefilter:
    drop_on_invalid_schema: true
    dedupe_window: 10s
  sampling:
    type: sticky
    base_rate: 0.05   # 5% global
    per_client_cap: 10req/s
    sticky_window: 3m
    rehydrate_window: 2m  # if late billing_key arrives within this window we up-sample
```

 anika: rehydrate_window is key for us. but we need an infra story: where does the late billing_key lookup happen? two options I see: (1) keep a fast ephemeral store in edge for rehydrate keys, (2) send sampled identifiers to a separate "candidate" stream that can be rejoined during enrichment. both have cost/complexity tradeoffs.

 todd: the ephemeral store seems simpler but is stateful at the edge and will be a pain for autoscaling. the candidate stream introduces cross-service joins and more pipeline complexity but centralizes state.

 kevin: what if we hybridize: small ephemeral LRU cache at edge for very short windows (30-120s) and also emit low-volume candidate stream for longer rehydration windows and auditing. that minimizes edge state while preserving rehydration.

 mira: sounds reasonable. action items:
- anika to list enrichment paths where billing_key is added and expected latency
- kevin to prototype edge config + LRU cache metrics (hit/miss)
- todd to pull noisy-client contribution numbers and simulate cost impact of base_rate 5% vs 10%

 ingest-bot: note: feature-flag rollout "obs-gating-v1" created and targeting canary infra tomorrow 07:00 UTC.

 anika: ack, I'll document the late-enrich flows by EOD.

 todd: I'll run the sim and post numbers in this thread. short follow-up: do we need an explicit opt-out for paying customers? some enterprise customers send large telemetry and would want white-listing.

 mira: yes — add allowlist/whitelist in config and tie to tenant id. also expose a console toggle. thanks all :thumbsup:
